Under the 20th Order (see post p.29),it will be seen
that the service, in order to enable the Plaintiff to appear
for the Defendant, may be at his dwelling house or usual
place of abode. Still it is apprehended that there must
be some good reason for omitting to make the personal
service. (See Pultney vs. Skelton, 5 Vesey, 147).
